audit.whatIsWrong: Every phases[N].side read 'Skill' while the content layer and the packet both read Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Skill/Hwei/Hwei, and phases[0..3].why described Hwei winning the very rows the content layer gave to Xerath.
audit.why: Xerath out-ranges Hwei's entire palette before items; a 48.27% win rate over 4038 games matches a losing early lane that recovers on the first-item spike.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-4 to Xerath with matching whys, level 6 Skill, first item and two items to Hwei.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike named a Xerath cooldown, so the 'wait for X before you Y' advice the packet flagged as missing was still absent.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s and Rite of the Arcane 130/115/100s — those two numbers are the whole green-light system.
audit.corrected: Windows now keyed to Shocking Orb's 13s rank-1 cooldown and his 130s ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rite of the Arcane was described as a zoning tool but never as a channel, and the page told you to hide behind minions from Arcanopulse.
audit.why: Riot's text says Rite of the Arcane immobilizes Xerath and the kit flags it as an interruptible channel — Grim Visage or Crushing Maw cancels it. Arcanopulse damages 'all targets hit', so it pierces minions and they never block it.
audit.corrected: Cancel Rite of the Arcane with an E paint; sidestep Arcanopulse rather than trying to body-block it.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and dosFull[2].d called Shocking Orb a fifteen-second cooldown.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1, 11s at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Both fields now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings under unrelated titles; wants.you[3] called the fear a W.
audit.why: Hwei's fear is Grim Visage, an E (Subject: Torment) paint, not a W.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to their titles and the fear named correctly.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E fear paint has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb: 13s at rank 1, 11s at rank 5 — his only CC, and his artillery converts into a kill only through it, so step up on its downtime. - Rite of the Arcane is a 130s channel: Grim Visage or Crushing Maw cancels it and the whole ultimate is gone.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Xerath wins by stunning you from 1050 with Shocking Orb, then converting with Eye of Destruction and a free Arcanopulse.

edits.before: Standing mid-cast-animation inside his engage range with the fear already spent — every assassin and fighter in the pool is waiting for exactly that frame.
edits.after: Standing still to line up a paint inside 1050 range — Shocking Orb lands on the cast animation and the stun buys him a full charged Arcanopulse.

edits.before: Carry through range — no mid pool champion paints a teamfight from further away; your R + QQ decides objectives before they start.
edits.after: Carry by deleting his ultimate — Rite of the Arcane roots him in place for 130 seconds of cooldown, and one E paint cancels the whole channel.

edits.before: If Xerath gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Shocking Orb (Stun) extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with QA clears and stay relevant through max-range poke.

notes: Real error corrected: the page told you to body-block Arcanopulse with minions, but Riot's text says it damages 'all targets hit', so it pierces and minions never block it. Chart disagreement resolved by moving the full layer onto the content layer and the packet, which agreed; phases[0..3].why were rewritten in the same proposal because they described Hwei winning rows that now belong to Xerath. No paired win[N] edits were possible — win[N] already carried the target values. Xerath's Q range in the kit reads 750, which is the uncharged minimum; I did not assert a charged maximum anywhere because the kit does not give one.
